creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Five reports converged on shell safety with five different spellings: `{x:q}`, `shell_quote()`, `{title!q}`, argv-form `$[...]`, and list-form `$cmd_list`. The review is explicit that they reduce to two orthogonal features and must not be averaged:

1. A quoting mechanism usable inside command strings. This is the p0-tier1 `shell_escape()` card and ships independently.
2. A shell-free argv form - safe by construction, but it gives up pipes, redirection, and everything else the shell provides.

The agent-facing report argues argv-form is the only option safe by construction; dev-longtail attaches the lost-shell-features caveat. `principles.md` ("no cryptic symbols") weighs against the `!q` spelling.

If a lint comes with it, taint-scope it. As sketched, "any interpolation inside `$` without `:q`" fires on nearly every shell command in the corpus - its critic called it a false-positive generator. Scope it to values from args, `input()`, HTTP, files, and subprocesses, or ship the primitive with no lint.
title: Decide the shell execution model: quoting primitive, argv form, or both
